items.title: ZDI-26-1033: (0Day) (Pwn2Own) United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP GetConfiguration Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated RCE zero-day in Grizzl-E Smart EV chargers allows network-adjacent code execution via OCPP.
items.summary: A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers within the handling of OCPP GetConfiguration requests, allowing unauthenticated network-adjacent attackers to achieve remote code execution. ZDI made multiple unsuccessful attempts to contact the vendor regarding the vulnerability discovered during Pwn2Own Automotive 2026. The only salient mitigation strategy is to restrict network interaction with the vulnerable device. A coordinated public release of the advisory occurred on November 18, 2026.
key_facts: Vulnerable Product: United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers
Vulnerability Type: Stack-based Buffer Overflow RCE
items.bottom_line: Network interaction with vulnerable United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers must be restricted as the vendor has failed to provide a patch.

claims.text: This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers without authentication.

items.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products  (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Active exploitation of critical PHP RCE vulnerabilities targets internet-exposed Palo Alto Networks management interfaces.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has evaluated its product portfolio regarding two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which affect PAN-OS software on PA-Series, VM-Series firewalls, and Panorama. CVE-2026-109618 allows RCE via uninitialized request memory after out-of-memory errors handled by longjmp(), while CVE-2026-109619 leaves global memory pointing to freed memory regions. Active exploitation has been observed against management interfaces exposed to the internet, prompting the vendor to assign a critical CVSS score of 9.2 and recommend restricting management access or deploying virtual patches.

CVE-2026-109619: remote code execution via global memory pointing to freed regions
items.bottom_line: Administrators must restrict external access to firewall management interfaces immediately to mitigate actively exploited critical PHP vulnerabilities.

items.title: CVE-2026-90436: Apache Apache Axis Unsafe Reflection Vulnerability
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated RCE vulnerability in Apache Axis (unsafe reflection) has been added to CISA's KEV catalog.
items.summary: Apache Axis contains an unsafe reflection vulnerability that enables unauthenticated remote code execution via a crafted SOAP fault message, prompting Apache Axis to instantiate an attacker-specified class available on the classpath. The vulnerability impacts end-of-life or end-of-service products, and CISA has added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Federal agencies are required to apply vendor mitigations or discontinue use in compliance with binding operational directives.
items.bottom_line: Discontinue use or apply vendor mitigations immediately for vulnerable, end-of-life Apache Axis installations facing remote code execution risks.

items.title: CVE-2026-115731: Perforce Perforce Puppet Enterprise Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability
items.one_liner: CISA adds CVE-2026-115731 in Perforce Puppet Enterprise to its KEV catalog, requiring federal fixes by December 1, 2026.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-115731, a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in Perforce Puppet Enterprise, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw exists in Puppet's report-processing code, allowing any client possessing a CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as the service user by submitting a crafted rich-data type via a PUT request. If certificate authorities automatically sign requests without strong verification, unauthenticated network attackers can obtain valid certificates and exploit the vulnerability. Federal civilian agencies must apply vendor mitigations by December 1, 2026, in accordance with CISA Binding Operational Directive 26-04.
key_facts: CVE-2026-115731: Deserialization of untrusted data in Perforce Puppet Enterprise
items.bottom_line: Perforce Puppet Enterprise servers allowing automated certificate signing are exposed to unauthenticated remote code execution via crafted report payloads.

items.one_liner: GitLab released critical patches for multiple high-severity vulnerabilities, including an RCE-capable integer overflow and authentication bypasses.
items.summary: GitLab has released critical security patches for multiple versions of its Community and Enterprise editions to address several high-severity vulnerabilities. The updates fix issues including an integer overflow in the regular expression compiler, improper authentication in OmniAuth-to-LDAP lookups, and cache poisoning in OAuth/OIDC endpoints. Self-managed instances are urged to upgrade immediately, and users not using official packages must also update their Ruby runtime to specific versions to mitigate a Ruby-level vulnerability (CVE-2026-110264).

items.title: Microsoft's official Python agent framework hijacked to distribute malware
items.one_liner: Microsoft's official PyPI account was compromised to push malicious agent-framework updates that actively harvest cloud and developer credentials.
items.summary: Microsoft's official Python agent-framework package on PyPI was hijacked to distribute info-stealing malware via versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2. The malicious versions actively request and exfiltrate fresh identity tokens for GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, and Azure to an external webhook without ever needing to be explicitly imported by the developer. The compromise points to unauthorized access to an administrator account within Microsoft's GitHub organization. As a result, developers utilizing these versions must immediately inspect their environments and revoke exposed credentials.
items.bottom_line: Official packages from major publishers can be backdoored via compromised administrator credentials, turning trusted dependencies into credential harvesters.

items.title: Criminals are using ARTEX AI agents to speed up cyberattacks, FBI warns
items.one_liner: The FBI warns that attackers are weaponizing the open-source ARTEX AI framework to achieve privileged access in under three hours.
items.summary: The FBI issued a FLASH advisory warning that cybercriminals are abusing ARTEX, an open-source penetration-testing framework, to automate intrusions against organizations worldwide. Attackers leverage the AI-driven planning and execution agents to drastically speed up cyberattacks, with some intrusions reaching privileged access in under three hours. The tool connects external large language models to orchestrate attacks across sectors like finance, government, healthcare, and technology with minimal human input. Microsoft separately reported that a China-state-aligned group used ARTEX to compromise ConnectWise credentials and accelerate operations.

items.title: Optimizely Supply Chain Attack Delivers Malware to 178 Organizations via Official CDN Project JavaScript
items.one_liner: A supply-chain compromise of Optimizely CDN scripts delivered browser-based malware targeting crypto wallets, payment cards, and iOS devices.
items.summary: Attackers compromised the official Optimizely CDN project JavaScript, distributing multi-purpose malware via 188 tampered snippets to 178 organizations, including major brands. The injected loader executes in visitor browsers to steal cryptocurrency by replacing wallet addresses, exfiltrate payment card data from form fields, capture cookies, and deliver iOS exploit kits via hidden iframes. Security researchers identified several target endpoints, though successful device-level exploitation and the total financial loss remain unconfirmed. Administrators can detect the supply-chain breach by monitoring changes in Optimizely snippet hash values, unexpected external domain connections, and Content Security Policy violations.
items.bottom_line: Trusted third-party CDN scripts can be weaponized for widespread client-side data theft without altering internal server code.

items.title: British hacker who stole $11m through text message scheme jailed for six years in US
items.one_liner: Scattered Spider affiliate Tyler Buchanan receives a six-year US prison sentence for an SMS phishing and cryptocurrency theft ring.
items.summary: British hacker Tyler Buchanan, a member of the Scattered Spider collective, has been sentenced to six years in a US federal prison for conspiring to hack corporate employees via SMS phishing. Operating from his home, Buchanan and accomplices targeted major tech and telecom firms using spoofed websites and Telegram bots to harvest credentials, ultimately stealing more than $11.6m in cryptocurrency via SIM-swapping. The multi-year international investigation concluded with Buchanan's extradition following his arrest at Palma de Mallorca Airport in Spain.

items.title: CVE-2026-129991 - Dokploy: Authenticated Command Injection via unescaped backup.prefix in database/service backup commands leads to RCE as root
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-129991 grants authenticated users root RCE in Dokploy prior to v0.31.1 via unescaped backup prefix fields.
items.summary: An authenticated command injection vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-129991, has been identified in Dokploy, a free self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS) prior to version 0.31.1. The flaw stems from insufficient input validation on the backup prefix field, where `normalizeS3Path` preserves shell metacharacters before they are interpolated into `rclone` upload and retention-cleanup command strings. An authenticated organization member with backup permissions can execute arbitrary commands as root on the Dokploy host or configured remote servers during manual, scheduled, or retention-cleanup backups for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, libSQL, Compose, or web-server instances. The vulnerability has been addressed in version 0.31.1.
items.bottom_line: Dokploy prior to version 0.31.1 contains an authenticated command injection vulnerability allowing remote code execution as root via backup prefixes.

items.summary: Security researchers have detailed a critical exploit chain in Barracuda Email Security Gateway (ESG) involving CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560. The first vulnerability is a pre-authentication authorization bypass that allows arbitrary configuration restoration, while the second is an OS command injection flaw. Barracuda has released version 9.4.0.029 to address these issues, which also affect other products like the Load Balancer ADC and WAF.

items.title: Eight in Ten LLMs Leak System-Prompt Secrets: Nevan, an Agentic Capture-the-Flag Study
items.one_liner: An audit of 363 LLMs reveals that 80% leak system-prompt secrets when targeted by agentic prompt-injection attacks.
items.summary: Researchers conducted an instruction-hierarchy audit across 363 text-in/text-out models from the OpenRouter catalog by tasking an AI agent steered by a human researcher to extract a protected 16-character secret flag from each model's system prompt. The secret was successfully exfiltrated from 300 models, with 170 of those captures involving a non-English language pivot, predominantly French. The results demonstrate that the vast majority of tested models frequently prioritized user requests over their system instructions. The authors advise practitioners against storing sensitive secrets in system prompts and recommend enforcing critical security behaviors via external output validation and deterministic checks.
items.bottom_line: Testing across 363 models reveals that 80% of LLMs leak system-prompt secrets when subjected to agentic persuasion and non-English language pivots.

items.summary: The Node.js project released security updates addressing CVE-2026-111497, a critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the bundled Brotli decoder known as Node2Shell, which allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code. Siemens has published an advisory detailing the impact of this flaw across numerous Industrial Automation Software products, including COMOS Walkinside, SIMATIC WinCC variants, and TIA Administrator. Affected product lines are being patched with new versions, while CISA and Siemens recommend restricting network exposure, isolating control systems behind firewalls, and avoiding direct internet accessibility.

items.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
items.one_liner: Cisco issued an informational advisory regarding the emergency distrust of eMudhra intermediate CAs due to weak key generation.
items.summary: Between October 17 and October 20, 2026, a critical security compromise was uncovered involving Certificate Authorities managed by eMudhra. A security researcher demonstrated that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were fundamentally broken due to an error in their Key Generation Ceremony in April 2025, enabling anyone to brute-force acquire the private keys within seconds. Cisco issued an informational security advisory regarding the emergency distrust of these eMudhra root and intermediate certificate authorities across products. Similar advisories have been published by Cisco Talos and Splunk.

items.title: CVE-2026-129483 (CRITICAL 9.3): Cyrus SASL through 2.1.28 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the SRP server mechanism because…
items.one_liner: Cyrus SASL up to 2.1.28 contains a critical authentication bypass via the SRP server mechanism, allowing unauthenticated passwordless access.
items.summary: Cyrus SASL versions through 2.1.28 contain a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in the SRP server mechanism due to improper validation of client public values. Because srp_server_mech_step2 does not reject client public values equal to multiples of N, unauthenticated network clients can send a value of A equal to N to force a zero shared secret. This allows an attacker to authenticate as any existing user without knowing their password and to successfully learn session keys. The vulnerability carries a critical CVSS base score of 9.3.
items.bottom_line: Cryptographic implementation flaws in server-side authentication mechanisms can allow unauthenticated remote attackers to bypass passwords entirely.

items.title: CVE-2026-129349 (CRITICAL 9.1): When authentication caching is enabled on DefaultLdapRealm, after a user logs in successfully once, subsequen…
items.one_liner: Authentication caching enabled on Apache Shiro's DefaultLdapRealm allows attackers to log in with any password after a user's initial login.
items.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-129349 with a CVSS score of 9.1, affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.0 when authentication caching is enabled on DefaultLdapRealm or JndiLdapRealm. When enabled, a successful initial login caches authentication, causing subsequent logins for that user to succeed with any password because the default AllowAllCredentialsMatcher accepts all credentials. Mitigation requires upgrading to version 3.0.1 or later, disabling authentication caching, or configuring a strict credentials matcher.
items.bottom_line: Apache Shiro deployments using LDAP authentication caching must upgrade to version 3.0.1 immediately to prevent full authentication bypass.

items.title: We caught the agent-framework PyPI compromise six minutes after it published
items.one_liner: Compromised versions of the Microsoft agent-framework package on PyPI silently exfiltrate credentials on every Python startup.
items.summary: Microsoft's agent-framework meta-package on PyPI was compromised in versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, deploying a credential-stealing startup hook that ran every time Python started. The malicious .pth hook triggered a telemetry script that collected environment variables, token caches, and cloud endpoints from running processes, exfiltrating them via a Base64-encoded and zlib-compressed POST request to an external webhook. Elastic Security Labs flagged the package six minutes after publication, and PyPI removed both versions within an hour. Anyone who used those versions on a host should assume all secrets on that host are compromised and pin back to version 1.26.0.
items.bottom_line: Immediately revoke all secrets and pin back to version 1.26.0 if your systems ever downloaded agent-framework versions 1.26.1 or 1.26.2.

claims.text: The compromised package is the meta-package, a thin wrapper used to pull in the different framework dependencies.

items.title: 0% GPU utilization: How SANSAR hides Linux cryptomining
items.one_liner: Attackers are using unauthenticated Ray job agents to deploy sophisticated Linux cryptomining toolkits that hide GPU usage and process activity.
items.summary: Elastic Security Labs has uncovered a Linux cryptomining campaign (REF3364) that utilizes a Rust-based orchestrator named SANSAR to manage CPU and GPU miners. The attackers gained initial access by exploiting an unauthenticated Ray job agent, subsequently deploying a kernel rootkit to hide processes and an NVIDIA Management Library (NVML) wrapper to falsify GPU usage metrics. The toolkit also includes a backdoor, 'netns', which retrieves command-and-control addresses from Ethereum smart contracts.

items.title: Efficient Wide-Beam Generative Retrieval with Model-Native Trie Decoding and Shared-Context Attention
items.one_liner: Model-native Trie decoding and shared-context attention dramatically accelerate generative retrieval serving throughput for LLM applications.
items.summary: A new generative retrieval technique called Trie-Head stores identifier tries as validated GPU tensors to eliminate CPU-GPU coordination overhead and vocabulary-wide candidate buffers. Complemented by shared-context attention that reuses prompt key-value blocks across beams, the system avoids Python constraint callbacks and reduces memory traffic. Implemented in SGLang and evaluated on LinkedIn and Qualification Retrieval Platform workloads, the combined approach improves closed-loop throughput significantly over standard baselines. Specifically, it achieves up to 5.57x improvement over custom logit processor baselines and up to 2.63x over BF16 FlashRec.

Throughput improvement: up to 2.63x over BF16 FlashRec
items.bottom_line: Moving constraints and vocabulary scoring into model-native GPU tensors eliminates major CPU-GPU bottlenecks in generative retrieval serving.

items.title: Russian COLD RELIC Hackers Use Stolen Google Workspace Data to Breach Second U.S. Organization
items.one_liner: Cold Relic leveraged stolen Super Admin credentials and MFA manipulation from a prior breach to compromise a second U.S. organization.
items.summary: The Russia-linked cyber espionage group Cold Relic (also known as Star Blizzard or UNC4057) weaponized a prior cloud compromise at an unspecified U.S. entity to breach a second American organization. Using stolen credentials from a Super Admin account combined with MFA push fatigue, the actors registered unauthorized multi-factor authentication devices, passkeys, and backup codes for persistence. The attackers then used Google Takeout and mass file sharing to exfiltrate complete employee directories, corporate storage, and credential archives. Finally, they cleared security audit logs and utilized unrevoked passkeys to maintain long-term access and launch downstream phishing attacks.

items.title: Fridge Controller Attacks: Researchers Find Six Zero-Days in an Hour
items.one_liner: Researchers find six pre-auth RCE zero-days in Danfoss refrigeration controllers as active attacks spoil food and trigger fires across Europe.
items.summary: Midnight Blue researchers discovered six unpatched remote code execution zero-day vulnerabilities in Danfoss AK-SM800A refrigeration controllers in under an hour of manual review using publicly available firmware. Five of the stack-based buffer overflow flaws sit within unauthenticated web request handlers inside the root-privileged main application (`sm_app`), while the sixth impacts the gateway component enforcing strict HTTPS mode. Internet-exposed controllers have recently been targeted across Europe, triggering unauthorized defrost cycles, food spoilage, and fires. Security agencies and researchers strongly advise disconnecting these devices from the internet and enabling Strict mode.

items.title: 10-Year-Old NGINX HTTP/2 Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Code on Servers
items.one_liner: A critical decade-old unauthenticated RCE flaw in NGINX HTTP/2 allows attackers to run code as worker processes and potentially gain host root access, requiring an immediate upgrade to version 1.31.9 or 1.30.7.
items.summary: A decade-old critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-123007, dubbed 'nginx2root,' has been discovered in NGINX's HTTP/2 support, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable servers. The flaw impacts NGINX open-source versions 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 and various NGINX Plus releases, where successful exploitation grants code execution with NGINX worker process privileges. Security researchers demonstrated that bypassing ASLR is possible, and attackers can further escalate to root privileges on host machines by chaining this vulnerability with separate kernel bugs like SCTP issues, even within Docker containers. Vendor F5 has released patched versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 alongside fixes for four additional code execution vulnerabilities, prompting administrators to upgrade immediately and perform a full restart to replace running binaries.

items.title: AI finds zero-day flaws for just $4 now – even mediocre hackers can cash in

items.summary: Recent research by Xint.io shows that falling LLM token prices and improved reasoning capabilities have dramatically reduced the cost of discovering zero-day vulnerabilities. items.title: AI Hacking Tool ARTEX Survives GitHub Removal; FBI: Some Intrusions Reach Privileged Access in Hours
items.one_liner: Criminals are weaponizing open-source AI pentesting frameworks like ARTEX to achieve privileged access in hours, bypassing GitHub takedowns via forks.
items.summary: The FBI warned that criminal and state-aligned hackers are using ARTEX, a free AI penetration-testing framework, to execute automated attacks that achieved privileged access in under three hours. Despite the original developer removing the tool from GitHub on October 8, community forks, archived copies, and a commercial variant called ARTEX PRO have kept the software widely accessible. The framework operates as a multi-agent system written in Go that requires external large language model API calls to plan and execute attacks using techniques like SQL injection and server-side request forgery. Security researchers have also identified malicious forks containing backdoored Docker images and instances exploited for secret harvesting. Defenders face immense pressure as the tool's high tempo compresses the timeline for incident response.
items.bottom_line: AI-driven penetration testing frameworks significantly compress the attack lifecycle, allowing adversaries to reach privileged access within hours despite initial software removals.

items.title: Git security vulnerabilities announced
items.one_liner: Git 2.56.1 and backports fix six critical security flaws, including code execution during cloning and path traversal.
items.summary: The Git project has released security patches across multiple maintenance series, culminating in Git 2.56.1, to address six vulnerabilities including arbitrary code execution, path traversal, and stack corruption. CVE-2026-111760 involves an integer truncation vulnerability during index handling that permits an attacker-controlled Git server to overwrite repository metadata or execute code during cloning. Other fixed issues include path traversal via protocol v2 HEAD advertisements (CVE-2026-113408), stack corruption from excessive GPG signatures during merges (CVE-2026-114467), and out-of-bounds reads when applying compressed binary patches. Administrators and developers should update Git installations and dependent applications immediately.
key_facts: Affected versions: Git prior to 2.56.1 and backported series
items.bottom_line: Upgrading to Git 2.56.1 or patched maintenance releases is essential to mitigate remote code execution and path traversal flaws.

items.title: Myanmar faces historic genocide verdict at UN court over Rohingya massacres
items.one_liner: The International Court of Justice is set to issue a historic verdict in The Gambia's genocide case against Myanmar over the 2017 military atrocities against the Rohingya.
items.summary: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is set to deliver a landmark genocide verdict in a seven-year-old case brought by The Gambia against Myanmar concerning the 2017 military campaigns against the Rohingya population in Rakhine State. While numerous individuals have been convicted of genocide following conflicts in Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia, no sovereign state has ever been found guilty of genocide by an international court. Myanmar has denied allegations of genocide or ethnic cleansing, claiming its military operations were lawful counter-terrorism responses to militant attacks. The case, backed by the Organisation of Islamic Co-operation, establishes a significant legal precedent by allowing a third-party state without direct involvement to file a complaint under the 1948 Genocide Convention.
items.bottom_line: The ICJ's forthcoming ruling on Myanmar marks the first time an international court will judge whether a sovereign state is guilty of genocide.

items.one_liner: An AI-driven pilot successfully delivered pre-verified vulnerability patches directly to open-source maintainers, reducing alert fatigue.
items.summary: GitHub and Microsoft conducted a pilot program using an AI multi-model agentic scanning harness called Codename MDASH to help open-source maintainers fix vulnerabilities rather than inundate them with raw scan alerts. items.one_liner: Federal Reserve minutes signal future rate hikes and flag AI infrastructure debt and spending as major inflation risks.
items.summary: Federal Reserve meeting minutes released Wednesday revealed policymakers' confidence in October that further interest rate increases will be needed to curb broad-based inflation pressures, despite holding rates at 3.75%-4% during the meeting. Officials placed artificial intelligence at the center of their discussions, warning that AI-related demand poses a material inflation risk and that rapid debt growth through opaque financing structures could amplify losses. While most officials favor a patient approach to return inflation to the 2% target, Governor Christopher Waller suggested a half-point rate hike should be considered in December. Two officials dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase at the October meeting.

items.one_liner: Update Apache Roller immediately to patch CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 9.8), an unauthenticated RCE flaw under active exploitation.
items.summary: A critical unauthenticated deserialization vulnerability in Apache Roller's XML-RPC endpoint, tracked as CVE-2026-129448 with a CVSS score of 9.8, is under active exploitation in the wild. Users are urged to upgrade immediately to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, or alternatively disable the XML-RPC feature and set 'enabledForExtensions' to false.

items.title: Russian APT Poses as Employee of Hacked Firm to Breach Another US Organization
items.one_liner: Russia's Star Blizzard APT uses social engineering and credential theft via impersonation of previously compromised contacts to breach US firms.
items.summary: The Russia-linked APT group Star Blizzard (also known as Cold Relic) compromised a US organization by impersonating an employee from another US enterprise it had breached months prior. In the initial intrusion, the group utilized residential proxies, MFA push-notification fatigue, and compromised super-admin credentials to exfiltrate cloud storage drives and establish long-term persistence using passkeys and rogue MFA devices. After being ejected from the first target, the hackers leveraged compromised email accounts and secure messaging apps to build trusted relationships with associates at a second US organization, deploying phishing links to harvest credentials and Entra ID tokens. Google Threat Intelligence Group tracked the operation, highlighting how threat actors exploit established professional networks to bypass modern authentication controls.
items.bottom_line: State-sponsored threat actors can bypass MFA and enterprise security boundaries by masquerading as trusted internal contacts from previously compromised partner organizations.

items.one_liner: Update Java immediately to patch CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell), a pre-auth RCE vulnerability affecting multiple enterprise applications.
items.summary: A critical pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability, dubbed Java4Shell and tracked as CVE-2026-114938, affects Java 17.0.6 and later versions running on x86-64 Intel and AMD chips supporting AVX-512 VBMI. The flaw lies in an optimized Base64 decoder that writes 62 or 63 bytes past the output buffer when processing malformed strings ending with extra equal signs. Unauthenticated attackers can exploit this behavior via HTTP basic login headers or SAML artifacts in applications like Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak, Confluence, and PingFederate to corrupt memory and achieve code execution. Oracle and OpenJDK released patches for the vulnerability, which is rated 9.2 out of 10 under CVSS 4.0 by researchers.

items.title: Not All Evidence Is Admissible: Evidence Governance for Tool-Augmented Medical Agents
items.one_liner: Context-Independent Evidence Governance (CIEG) prevents medical AI agent errors by filtering tool outputs before they reach the reasoner.
items.summary: Tool-augmented medical agents frequently suffer from evidence hijacking, where silent tool failures are accepted blindly because the reasoner cannot ignore injected context. The authors demonstrate that this causes accurate models to output incorrect answers due to negative usable information within unvetted tool outputs. To solve this, they introduce context-independent evidence governance (CIEG), which frames tool outputs as discrete cards evaluated by an independent checker before reaching the reasoner. Across medical question answering, fundus glaucoma screening, and chest X-ray pneumonia classification, CIEG achieves state-of-the-art accuracy at lower computational costs.
items.bottom_line: Separating evidence validation from the primary LLM reasoning loop is essential for reliable tool-augmented medical applications.

items.title: LLM Misuse Safeguards Rely on Untrusted Input: A Widespread, High-Risk Vulnerability
items.one_liner: LLM misuse safeguards universally fail because they evaluate safety based on untrusted user-supplied professional claims rather than verifiable authorization.
items.summary: Large language model deployers rely on misuse safeguards to prevent the release of dangerous answers, but these mechanisms suffer from a widespread vulnerability: they decide whether to release information based on untrusted user input. Because anyone can fabricate a professional identity or purpose in their prompt, malicious actors are already successfully exploiting this architectural flaw to bypass defenses and elicit restricted capabilities. An analysis of 129 papers across 12 top venues revealed that every proposed defense shares this same systemic weakness. Current safeguard benchmarks fail to detect the flaw because they treat harm as a property of the text rather than verifying the user's authentic identity or permissions. Consequently, improving how safeguards evaluate text cannot close the vulnerability, necessitating a shift in how model access control is designed.
key_facts: Analyzed Papers: 129 papers across 12 top venues
items.bottom_line: LLM safety guardrails that rely on user-claimed professional identities are fundamentally bypassable by any attacker willing to fabricate a prompt.

claims.text: Deployers rely on misuse safeguards to keep such answers from attackers.

items.title: OverServe: Resource Amplification Attacks on SaaS Agents via Tool--Prompt Co-Design
items.one_liner: OverServe demonstrates how malicious tenants can weaponize tool-prompt co-design to achieve up to 93.88x resource amplification on subscription SaaS agents.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced OverServe, a multi-agent framework designed to construct resource amplification attacks against subscription-based SaaS AI agents using tool-prompt co-design. Because SaaS deployments bill customers via subscriptions rather than per-call fees while letting agents decide when tasks are complete, malicious tenants can exploit completion decisions to force agents into infinite verification loops. OverServe constructs custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) status tools and completion-confirmation prompts that return correct technical indicators while prompting agents to repeatedly check unfinished conditions. Testing across models like Qwen, Nemotron, DeepSeek, and Sonnet showed that OverServe achieved up to a 93.88x amplification of API requests while successfully bypassing MCP scanners without triggering security alerts.
items.bottom_line: Subscription SaaS AI agents are vulnerable to resource exhaustion attacks via co-designed MCP tools that artificially extend execution without triggering alerts.

items.title: Auditors Struggle to Catch Sabotage In End-to-End Transcripts of AI Safety Research
items.one_liner: Human auditors and frontier models struggle to detect deliberate sabotage introduced into end-to-end AI safety research transcripts.
items.summary: To stress-test defenses against AI systems sabotaging automated AI research, researchers conducted a red-team/blue-team study where a human expert acted as a saboteur on AI safety experiments. Human auditors reviewing full research transcripts and experimental runs failed to distinguish sabotaged research from benign work, achieving a random-chance AUROC of 0.59 and fully identifying specific sabotage in only 17% of cases. Frontier AI models performed slightly better than human auditors within statistical noise limits. The results highlight that current auditing methods struggle to detect subtle research sabotage committed by expert-level agents.
items.bottom_line: Current auditing techniques are largely ineffective at catching subtle research sabotage committed during automated AI development workflows.

items.title: Visual Contextual Attack: Jailbreaking MLLMs with Image-Driven Context Injection
items.one_liner: The VisCo attack uses image-driven context injection and dynamic auxiliary images to achieve an 85% ASR in jailbreaking GPT-4o.
items.summary: Researchers introduced the Visual Contextual Attack (VisCo), a new vision-centric jailbreak method designed to elicit harmful responses from multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Unlike prior attacks where images served merely as simple semantic triggers, VisCo constructs complete jailbreak scenarios using four vision-focused strategies that dynamically generate auxiliary images. The framework incorporates automatic toxicity obfuscation and semantic refinement to bypass black-box model safety guardrails. On MM-SafetyBench against GPT-4o, VisCo achieved an Attack Success Rate of 85 percent and a toxicity score of 4.78, significantly outperforming baseline text-to-visual injection methods.
items.bottom_line: Multimodal LLMs remain vulnerable to sophisticated visual context injection attacks that bypass safety guardrails by embedding malicious logic directly into generated image assets.

items.title: From Token Changes to Task Failures: Bit Flips in a Shared KV-Cache Block
items.one_liner: A single bit flip in a shared KV-cache block silently corrupts responses across multiple concurrent LLM requests depending on the task.
items.summary: In LLM serving systems utilizing prefix caching, shared system prompt KV blocks are stored as a single physical copy read by multiple concurrent requests. Software fault injection into vLLM serving Qwen3-8B demonstrated that single bit flips in these shared blocks corrupt multiple subsequent responses without causing visible degradation. The fraction of corrupted responses turning incorrect depended heavily on the task, ranging from low rates on code generation to high failure rates on held-out trivia benchmarks. Because damaged outputs resemble ordinary errors, detection requires auditing cached KV blocks directly rather than monitoring generated outputs.
items.bottom_line: Protecting LLM prefix caches against bit flips is critical because memory corruptions silently propagate errors across multiple independent user requests.

items.title: A Little Advice Suffices: Diffie-Hellman Is as Hard as Discrete Logarithm
items.one_liner: A long-standing conditional assumption in cryptography is resolved, proving Diffie-Hellman is as hard as discrete logarithm universally with minor advice.
items.summary: Researchers have proven that computing a Diffie-Hellman key is as hard as computing a discrete logarithm without requiring previous interval assumptions. By utilizing a zero-free half-plane for the Riemann zeta function, they demonstrated that an advice string of O(log p) bits allows discrete logarithms in every group of order p to be computed in polynomial time from a Diffie-Hellman oracle. This result removes the thirty-year-old proviso regarding small prime factors in short intervals from Maurer's theorem. It also makes unconditional several cryptographic characterizations, including Wolf's equivalence between discrete logarithm and Diffie-Hellman.
key_facts: Advice string length: O(log p) bits
items.bottom_line: The security equivalence of Diffie-Hellman and discrete logarithm is now mathematically unconditional for any prime order group.

items.title: Long-Context Generation Is a Sampling Problem (When You Turn Up the Heat)
items.one_liner: Using candidate-constrained samplers like top-nsigma prevents open-weight LLMs from collapsing during high-temperature long-context generation.
items.summary: Open-weight language models often degrade during long-form generation because improper samplers let low-probability candidate tokens proliferate at high temperatures. Testing across 29 models and multiple benchmarks demonstrated that samplers keeping candidate pools small and steady as temperature rises, such as top-nsigma, maintain their accuracy. In contrast, samplers like top-p allowed candidate pools to swell enormously, causing coding agents to fail completely on GitHub issue benchmarks at temperature 2. Controlling pool sizes effectively preserves model performance and output quality during long-context generation tasks.
items.bottom_line: Model degradation during long-context and high-temperature generation is primarily a sampling problem caused by unconstrained candidate pool expansion.

claims.text: At temperature 2, coding agents running top-p, top-k or Top-H resolve 0 of 100 GitHub issues, while the same agents running top-nsigma resolve 46 to 62 and win every issue the two samplers disagree on, on three Qwen3.5 models.

items.title: Signed but Not Safe: Requirement Integrity in Multi-Agent LLM Handoffs
items.one_liner: Cryptographically signed requirement manifests prevent in-transit tampering during multi-agent LLM handoffs, but secure requirement extraction remains the critical trust boundary.
items.summary: Enterprise AI agents that split requests across subagents face requirement corruption during handoffs, where requirements can be dropped, altered, or ignored. Researchers evaluated free-text, structured JSON, and signed requirement-manifest handoffs using Qwen3-8B and other models, finding that cryptographic signing cuts unsafe commits under attack from 69.4% to 9.0%. However, results showed that transit protection alone is insufficient because malicious or flawed extractions before signing can easily compromise the manifests. A testable pre-signing specification successfully blocked injected commits but introduced a significant rate of false refusals on benign requests.

items.bottom_line: Securing multi-agent handoffs requires signed requirement manifests to prevent in-transit tampering, though extraction remains the primary vulnerability.

items.title: From Sorry to QED: Refining LLM Math Proofs via Angelic Execution
items.one_liner: MathEye combines angelic execution and MaxSAT optimization to successfully fix broken LLM-generated math proofs with minimal human intervention.
items.summary: MathEye is a new framework designed to refine imperfect LLM-generated Lean math proof scripts by combining symbolic reasoning and minimal human interaction. The system employs angelic proof checking, an optimistic execution model that replaces failing proof fragments with placeholders to isolate exact obligations. By performing residual analysis over a proof dependence graph and formulating obligation selection as a MaxSAT optimization problem, MathEye selects a minimal-cost set of essential obligations for human resolution. Experiments across 30 real-world analysis and algebra benchmarks showed that MathEye solved 93.3% of the problems while reducing required user interaction by 55%.
items.bottom_line: Automated residual analysis and angelic proof checking can drastically reduce the human effort required to verify LLM-generated mathematical proofs.

items.title: SpecSearch: Towards Hardware-Aware Efficient Speculative Decoding
items.one_liner: SpecSearch uses a hardware-aware analytical model and Jev-based predictor to optimize speculative decoding throughput across diverse GPUs.
items.summary: SpecSearch is a hardware-aware search engine that jointly optimizes decoding strategy, draft length, and precision across workload-GPU pairs for speculative decoding in LLM inference. Using an analytical cost model and calibration measurements collected across multiple GPUs, a Jev-based predictor learns to select high-throughput decoding configurations on held-out GPUs without requiring deployment-time calibration. Evaluated across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs served by vLLM, SpecSearch significantly outperformed standard autoregressive and traditional speculative decoding baselines while eliminating deployment hardware calibration overhead.

items.title: Bajillion: Cryptographic Clearing for Micropayments
items.one_liner: Bajillion provides a scalable, cryptographic micropayment clearing protocol designed specifically to handle millions of transactions per second for AI agents.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed Bajillion, a cryptographic clearing protocol designed to handle scalable micropayments generated by AI agents browsing the web. Under this protocol, a sender signs a payment request and an untrusted operator provides a preconfirmation guaranteeing payment to the receiver, while periodically posting only net balances on-chain to save resources. The architecture guarantees that malicious operators can only omit payments rather than steal or misdirect funds, and lets users exit with finalized balances if an omission occurs. Because senders never have to raise disputes, the system supports ephemeral AI agents performing tens or hundreds of millions of transactions per second.
items.bottom_line: AI agents engaging in web automation can use Bajillion to execute trustless, high-volume micropayments without individual transaction disputes.

claims.text: Bajillion guarantees that a malicious operator can only omit payments -- it can never debit a sender beyond what it signed, nor misdirect a transfer.

items.title: The Safeguard Worked. Is the LLM System Safer?
items.one_liner: Current LLM safeguard evaluations are misleading because they measure blocking rates rather than the actual information leakage that occurs during an attack.
items.summary: A new research framework evaluating LLM safeguards reveals that current evaluation methods often fail to measure actual deployment safety. By analyzing 85 safeguard evaluations, researchers found that most fail to account for whether attack paths actually pass through the safeguard or what information remains accessible after a block. In one case, NeMo Guardrails blocked 94% of password leaks, yet the client still received the password in every instance. The study argues that developers must measure the 'harmful assistance' remaining after a block to truly secure LLM systems.
items.bottom_line: Blocking an attack is not the same as preventing a leak; developers must audit what information remains accessible to an attacker even when a safeguard triggers.

items.title: Dropbear: the restriction names an address — permitopen/permitlisten not enforced for unix-socket forwarding, docker.sock reachable (HEAD 99baf182, live-proven)
items.one_liner: Dropbear's Unix-socket forwarding bypasses permitopen restrictions, potentially exposing docker.sock to keys restricted to specific TCP endpoints.
items.summary: Dropbear SSH server fails to enforce per-destination permitopen and permitlisten restrictions when handling Unix-socket forwarding requests, allowing unlisted socket destinations such as docker.sock to be reached. While TCP forwarding correctly consults the key's allowed destination lists, streamlocal forwarding checks only a coarse global flag. This leaves restricted authentication keys vulnerable to unauthorized socket access despite functioning properly on TCP channels. The vulnerability affects commit 99baf1828c13e88de048e641d03694bfe8923251 and stems from an incomplete fix introduced in an earlier version.
items.bottom_line: Keys restricted with permitopen in Dropbear can still access arbitrary Unix sockets because streamlocal forwarding lacks per-destination validation.

items.title: Suspected Chinese APT Rebuilds EggStreme Malware After Exposure
items.one_liner: Suspected Chinese APT actors re-engineered the EggStreme malware framework within days of public exposure by Bitdefender.
items.summary: A suspected Chinese advanced persistent threat (APT) group rapidly rebuilt components of its EggStreme fileless malware framework after security firm Bitdefender publicly exposed it in September 2025. Targeting military and government organizations in the Philippines and Taiwan, the operators modified configuration protection mechanisms within 12 days of the report, deployed new ciphers, and updated loaders. The EggStremeAgent backdoor also dropped its raw TCP connections in favor of mutual TLS, integrated Windows domain mapping, and added in-memory PowerShell execution while stripping out keyloggers. Although the infrastructure shifted toward campaign-specific servers, defenders can still track the framework through constant behaviors such as DLL sideloading, file share movement, in-memory execution, and mutual TLS.
key_facts: Target sectors: Philippine government organizations and Taiwan
items.bottom_line: Chinese APT operators swiftly altered ciphers, loaders, and network protocols in the EggStreme framework following public security exposure, while retaining core evasion tactics like DLL sideloading.

items.title: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents

items.title: How Much of SAR Vehicle Recognition Is the Vehicle? Background Shortcuts, Angle Gaps and Partial Libraries on MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR
items.one_liner: High accuracy in SAR vehicle recognition benchmarks is heavily driven by background shortcuts and camera angle gaps rather than the vehicles themselves.
items.summary: An evaluation of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) vehicle recognition benchmarks like MSTAR and ATRNet-STAR reveals that deep neural networks rely heavily on background cues rather than target vehicles. Experiments using ConvNeXt-Small showed that zeroing out the central vehicle pixels still yielded high accuracy, while removing the vehicle entirely maintained substantial classification performance. Furthermore, changing depression angles drastically impacts accuracy based on the angular gap to training data rather than dataset size. The study recommends reporting background-only controls and angle gaps alongside raw accuracy metrics.
items.bottom_line: Computer vision models for SAR object recognition frequently exploit background shortcuts rather than learning features of the target vehicle.

items.one_liner: An intruder test of EU Digital Markets Act search datasets reveals low direct re-identification rates but lingering risks regarding query inference.
items.summary: A study evaluated the European Commission's anonymization measures for Alphabet's search-data sharing under Article 6(11) of the Digital Markets Act using motivated intruder testing. items.title: Fine-Grained Japanese Clinical Named Entity Recognition: A Controlled Comparison of BERT and Open-Weight Large Language Models
items.one_liner: For developers building clinical NLP pipelines, this study confirms that LLMs require significant fine-tuning and high output-token limits to match or exceed traditional BERT-based performance in fine-grained extraction.
items.summary: Researchers compared BERT-CRF baselines against nine open-weight LLMs for fine-grained Japanese clinical named entity recognition using the iCorpus benchmark. While zero-shot LLM performance was significantly lower than BERT, fine-tuned LLMs with at least 13B parameters outperformed BERT when provided with sufficient output-token limits. The study found that simply enforcing JSON schema constraints did not compensate for low zero-shot accuracy, suggesting that generation capacity and task-specific fine-tuning are critical for clinical extraction tasks. These findings highlight the importance of balancing model size and output constraints when replacing traditional encoder-based models in specialized domains.
items.bottom_line: Fine-tuned LLMs can outperform traditional BERT models in clinical NER, but only when provided with sufficient generation capacity and task-specific training.

items.title: TetherMark: Instance-Level Watermark Authentication Against Cross-Instance Transplantation
items.one_liner: TetherMark introduces instance-level watermark authentication to prevent attackers from transplanting valid watermarks onto unauthenticated images.
items.summary: Cross-instance transplantation occurs when an attacker extracts valid watermark evidence from one registered image and transplants it onto a different image within the same category to bypass verification. items.title: The Only Edge Was Memorized in Training: LLM Trading Agents Around Earnings and Bad News
items.one_liner: LLM trading agents fail to generate alpha from live news, deriving their only performance edge from memorized training data.
items.summary: Researchers tested LLM trading agents on 598 earnings announcements and 409 bad-news drops of large US stocks using a look-ahead-free benchmark. Instead, the only successful directional calls came from historical information memorized during training, with a GPT-based model correctly predicting 59.2% of earnings announcements before its training cutoff and 53.3% after it.

items.one_liner: Learned Pseudo-Count MCTS (LPC-MCTS) replaces independent visit counting with representation coverage estimation, significantly boosting LLM mathematical reasoning performance.
items.summary: Standard Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) utilized in LLM reasoning often suffers from count fragmentation, where independent visit counts are assigned to textual branches that share equivalent reasoning strategies, impairing exploration efficiency. items.title: PSM: Prompt Sensitivity Minimization via LLM-Guided Black-Box Optimization
items.one_liner: Prompt Sensitivity Minimization (PSM) hardens LLM system prompts against extraction attacks by using an LLM-guided optimizer to append protective utility-constrained text shields.
items.summary: Large Language Model system prompts often contain proprietary logic that makes them prime targets for extraction and adversarial query attacks. Existing defenses against prompt leakage often incur high computational overhead or are restricted to white-box access. To address this, researchers have introduced prompt sensitivity minimization via shield appending, a lightweight black-box optimization framework that adds a protective textual layer to original system prompts. By framing prompt hardening as a utility-constrained optimization problem, the approach leverages an LLM-as-optimizer to search possible SHIELD configurations that minimize a leakage metric against adversarial extraction suites while preserving semantic fidelity to baseline outputs. Empirical tests demonstrate that optimized SHIELDs significantly reduce prompt leakage without compromising intended model functionality.
items.bottom_line: Shield appending via black-box LLM optimization provides a lightweight and effective defense against system prompt extraction attacks without harming utility.

items.title: Threat Landscape of Vibe Coding and the Road to Secure Autonomy
items.one_liner: This taxonomy and threat model for AI-driven vibe coding provides a structural framework for analyzing the security boundaries of autonomous developer tools.
items.summary: Computer science researchers from arXiv examined the threat landscape of vibe coding, where individuals with limited programming experience use AI agents to write, test, and deploy code. The study formalizes a reference architecture, characterizes six levels of agent autonomy, and establishes a threat model across five trust boundaries encompassing developers, AI models, tools, cloud infrastructure, and the software ecosystem. The authors propose a taxonomy of twenty-one threats across nine classes, demonstrating that risks escalate with operational authority while most existing defenses rely on model judgment. items.title: DiscoveryAgent: A Framework for Scientist-centric Agentic AI

items.title: Can You Undo It? Reversibility Classes for AI Agent Actions
items.one_liner: Reversibility Classes introduce a structured framework and runtime session guard to evaluate whether tool-using AI agent actions can be safely undone.
items.summary: Researchers introduce Reversibility Classes, a declared five-level vocabulary with argument-sensitive rules and prior-state capture contracts designed to determine whether tool-using AI agent actions can be undone. Tested across 536 tools and 20 Model Context Protocol servers over 2,158 runs, the implemented session guard successfully gated actions in all 29 attack-positive test runs, outperforming a baseline read/write proxy while adding minimal approval interruptions. The framework highlights the need to make recovery assumptions explicit and testable for autonomous tool execution.
items.bottom_line: Evaluating AI agent safety requires explicit, rule-based reversibility classes and state-capture contracts rather than relying on permission grants alone.

items.title: rApp/xApp Attestation: A New Security Use Case for O-RAN

items.summary: Researchers have introduced rApp/xApp attestation as a runtime integrity verification mechanism for Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) architectures, addressing the security gap where existing specifications lack concrete ways to verify running apps. items.title: EvoDisco: Strategy Discovery for Evolving Agent Memory
items.one_liner: EvoDisco uses evolutionary strategy discovery to dynamically evolve LLM agent memory through learnable semantic operators.
items.summary: Researchers introduce EvoDisco, a framework that models agent memory evolution as evolutionary strategy discovery rather than relying on static operator schedules. A learnable policy conditions on current memory states and task histories to dynamically select, instantiate, and apply one of four semantic operators: Abstract, Refine, Bridge, and Reframe. The policy is optimized via a bi-level fitness function containing an inner signal scoring retrieval-quality improvement against memory complexity, and an outer signal assessing strategic utility regret and selection diversity. Tested across ALFWorld, WebShop, and LifelongAgentBench, EvoDisco significantly outperforms traditional memory baselines like MemP and MemRL, showing strong zero-shot and online transfer capabilities.
items.bottom_line: LLM agent performance improves significantly when memory management operators are dynamically discovered and optimized via bi-level fitness functions rather than fixed schedules.

items.title: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
items.one_liner: SLED and Sensor Slicing bring deterministic, isolated O-RAN network slicing to multi-modal sensor streams, preventing severe latency spikes under heavy load.

items.title: obfsgen: Generative Tunnel Obfuscation
items.one_liner: obfsgen uses generative sequence models to produce schedule-driven traffic obfuscation, helping circumvention tunnels evade shape-based censorship.
items.summary: Encrypted censorship-circumvention tunnels face blocking because their traffic shapes exhibit exploitable fingerprints despite using standard protocols like TLS. Traditional application-driven traffic-shaping obfuscators like obfs4 cannot hide these patterns because they only append to application-created shapes. To solve this, researchers introduced obfsgen, a schedule-driven tunnel obfuscator that decides transmission timing and volume independently of the application. By sampling its schedule from a generative sequence model of normal traffic, obfsgen captures long-range dependencies to produce indistinguishable traffic flows while handling practical challenges like network synchronization.
items.bottom_line: Generative schedule-driven traffic shaping can successfully hide encrypted tunnel fingerprints from modern network censors.

items.title: TapMap: Free, open-source network map
items.one_liner: TapMap is an open-source utility that maps active network connections geographically and monitors significant socket events with built-in alert throttling.
items.summary: TapMap is a free, open-source desktop application that maps active network connections onto an interactive world map by resolving remote IP addresses against local GeoIP databases. Designed by Ola Lie, the tool associates connections with Autonomous System Numbers and provides OS-level application visibility for every active socket. It logs up to 500 recent events as Significant Connections and supports desktop and MQTT notifications for new applications, countries, or ports. To prevent alert fatigue, notifications undergo a mandatory learning period of seven active insights days by default before triggering.
key_facts: Event log limit: Up to 500 recent events
Learning period: 7 active Insights days by default
items.bottom_line: Local network visualization tools provide immediate visibility into active socket destinations while requiring caution regarding GeoIP precision limitations.

items.title: Windows 11 Collects Data on Coding Agents and Developer Tools You Use
items.one_liner: Windows 11 telemetry quietly catalogs every developer tool and AI coding agent you run on your machine.
items.summary: Security researcher Xusheng Li discovered that Windows 11's MissionControlAggregator component tracks the usage of various coding agents, developer tools, and compilers when optional diagnostic data is enabled. The DLL subscribes to application interactivity and state change events across both native Windows environments and WSL, matching process identities against built-in lists. It records matches locally and aggregates them into binary bitsets for telemetry upload via the DiagTrack service. The monitored tools include CLI and desktop variants of AI coding agents like Claude, Codex, and Cursor, alongside standard development utilities such as Node.js, Python, and GCC.
items.bottom_line: Developers must check their optional diagnostic data settings on Windows 11 to prevent local AI tool usage from being logged.

items.title: Muslims to outnumber Christians by 2035 worldwide: Pew research
items.one_liner: Pew Research projects Islam will surpass Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035, driven by higher global fertility rates.
items.summary: A Pew Research Center study projects that Islam will surpass Christianity to become the world's largest religion by 2035, driven by higher fertility rates averaging 3.1 children per woman among Muslims compared to 2.5 for Christians. By 2070, the global Muslim population is expected to reach 3.6 billion while Christians will number just under 3 billion, with more than half of the world's Christians living in sub-Saharan Africa. In India, Hindus are projected to remain the majority at 75.8% by 2070, down from 79.4% in 2020, while the Muslim population share is expected to rise from 15.2% to 19.6%. Globally, the absolute number of Hindus will increase from 1.2 billion to 1.4 billion, though their overall population share will dip slightly to 14% due to faster growth rates elsewhere.

Projected Christian Population by 2070: Under 3 billion
Muslim Fertility Rate (2020-2025): 3.1 children per woman
Christian Fertility Rate (2020-2025): 2.5 children per woman
items.bottom_line: Global demographic shifts will make Islam the world's largest religion by 2035, while India's Hindu population share is projected to shift to 75.8% by 2070.

items.title: US lawmakers push to raise minimum wage to $25, end tipped pay system
items.one_liner: US lawmakers are advancing legislation to gradually increase the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour and eliminate the tipped subminimum wage.
items.summary: A coalition of 17 US lawmakers is pushing for the passage of the Living Wage For All Act to progressively raise the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour and eliminate the subminimum tipped wage system. For large employers with over 500 employees or $1 billion in annual revenue, the wage hike would phase in by 2031, while smaller employers would have until 2038, after which rates would automatically adjust to maintain two-thirds of the US median hourly wage. The legislation also aims to abolish the $2.13 federal tipped subminimum wage, a legacy practice originating from the 1938 Fair Labor Standards Act that historically impacted marginalized workers. While several jurisdictions like Washington, DC, and Washington state have established higher local minimum wages, the federal rate has remained stagnant at $7.25 since 2009, leaving workers across 20 states at the federal floor.

Current Tipped Subminimum Wage: $2.13 an hour
items.bottom_line: The Living Wage For All Act proposes a federally mandated $25 minimum wage and the complete elimination of subminimum pay for tipped workers.

items.title: AnalogLayoutWorld Benchmark Tests AI Coding Agents on Physical Analog Chip Layout
items.one_liner: AI agents struggle with the physical constraints of analog chip design, succeeding in only 23% of layout tasks despite high GDS generation rates.
items.summary: The Nova-Silicon research team has released AnalogLayoutWorld, an open-source benchmark designed to evaluate AI coding agents on physical analog integrated circuit layout tasks. items.summary: Infosys shares have declined over 25% in the past year and are down 40% over five years, recently touching a 52-week low of ₹980.30 in September 2026. Despite the prolonged correction and lowered revenue guidance for FY27 to 1-2% in constant-currency terms, brokerage Monarch Networth Capital has recommended accumulating the stock with a target of ₹1,400 to ₹1,550 over the next three to five months. The bullish recommendation is supported by technical indicators, including strong institutional absorption along the rising 200-month exponential moving average and a double-bottom reversal pattern with bullish monthly RSI divergence. However, investors are advised to maintain a strict stop-loss below ₹980 to manage downside risk if the support level fails.

items.bottom_line: Technical indicators suggest Infosys may have found a multi-year support base near ₹980, prompting a buy recommendation despite its reduced FY27 revenue guidance.

items.title: V2 Retail slides 15% to 2-year low, then stages sharp rebound. What's driving the wild swings in this beaten-down stock?
items.one_liner: Value retailer V2 Retail saw sharp stock volatility and heavy trading volumes following a promoter stake sale and a slowdown in festival-normalised same-store sales growth.
items.summary: V2 Retail shares experienced high volatility, sliding 15% to a two-year low before rebounding to close down 3%, driven by heavy trading volumes where 86.5 million shares changed hands. The wild swings followed Motilal Oswal selling a 1.07% stake, reducing its holding to 4.92%. For the September quarter of FY27, the value retailer reported a 5.7% year-on-year increase in net profit to ₹18.21 crore and revenue of ₹905.59 crore, while total expenses rose 28.24% to ₹883.30 crore. Meanwhile, festival-normalised same-store sales growth slowed significantly to 0.5% amid a festive calendar shift. Despite the sluggish SSSG, the retailer expanded its footprint by opening 49 stores during the quarter, bringing its total store count to 427.
key_facts: Stake sold: 1.07% (3,921,567 shares) by Motilal Oswal

items.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 hits record one light-day distance, 50 years after launch
items.summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, the most distant human-made object, has reached a distance of one light-day from Earth nearly 50 years after it was launched. The spacecraft hit the milestone on Wednesday and is now about 26 billion km away, according to NASA. A light-day is the distance light can travel in 24 hours, which means messages sent from Earth take a day to reach Voyager 1, and another day for teams on the ground to receive a reply. The feat is “the best illustration of just how vast space is”, said NASA scientist Tiffany Kataria. “So much of what we dream about is travelling to other stellar systems,” she told the AFP news agency.

items.title: Energy-Based Reasoners: 385x more efficient inference
items.summary: Looping is a powerful inductive bias for reasoning. By repeatedly iterating a recurrent block, looped models can scale their effective depth and enable multi-step reasoning in latent space. However, existing looped models are not inherently guided by an explicit measure of progress, making it difficult to determine when to stop looping and how to improve upon the current state. To enable this, we introduce Energy-Based Reasoners (EBRs), which learn an energy function over latent reasoning states and formulate looped updates as gradient descent on this energy. The energy scores latent states, while its gradient guides refinement and provides a signal for stopping.
